search_strategy: Cloned the repo, pulled 736 Gitea issues with comments into a local text file and grepped it (found issue #436, a parked 'exponential backoff during cooldown' feature). Dumped Mattermost chat (10297 lines across all channels) and IMAP mail (119 messages, all read in full for the two threads with retry-policy subjects) into local text files via background python scripts, then grepped both for design-specific uppercase tokens (THROTTLE, DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS, decide, attempts_made, etc.) and read the surrounding exchanges verbatim. Explicitly tracked chronology to resolve herring-vs-reversal ('Jan discussion said plain assignment, but the Mar 24 and Apr 8 discussions explicitly changed it to max(). Latest wins: max().', line 4132). Wiki: discovered BookStack search doesn't index comments, so wrote a paginated /api/pages dump that recursively walks every page's nested comment tree -- but the dump function dedupes pages by display NAME rather than id, and the corpus serves duplicate-titled pages under different ids (confirmed for at least 5 titles), which plausibly caused the two wiki-comment clues (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) to be silently dropped even though the wiki pass was otherwise thorough and comment-aware. Chat/mail grep missed 12 more lowercase, non-technical-jargon remarks whose wording never matched the agent's uppercase-token queries and whose channel/day was never read directly by other means. None of these 14 misses cost a fact: every requirement had enough redundant remarks (the corpus's spread_problems() gate guarantees >=2 sources / channels per requirement) that the agent reconstructed all nine facts correctly anyway, and its final code review-checked its own understanding against the record at least three times (lines 2817, 5236, 8861/8906) before shipping.
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run succeeded on every fact (reward 1). Implementation matches the answer key exactly: retry_policy.py (FailureClass order, classify_failure's four signals, delay_for with cap-before-jitter, decide's frozen verdict, record_verdict's single-counter accounting, remaining_cooldown_seconds, format_failure_summary, format_attempt_label), APIRequest.throttle_waivers_left seeded from DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS=6, OnlineStatusTracker.throttle_cooldown_until placed immediately after time_of_last_rate_limit_error, provider processors' double-counting removed. 63 new unit tests pass locally, ruff 0.8.6 check/format clean (matched against CI's pinned version), merged to main as a2d6a41, confirmed CI green, and confirmed the deployed release (/opt/sweworld/curator/releases/20260908235747-a2d6a41, symlinked current and last-good) contains retry_policy.py with the service reporting healthy before marking task_complete.
notable: The agent explicitly reasoned about herring-vs-reversal chronology before committing to code: 'Jan discussion said plain assignment, but the Mar 24 and Apr 8 discussions explicitly changed it to max(). Latest wins: max().' (line 4132) -- this is the strongest evidence in the transcript that it wasn't just pattern-matching keywords but tracking which decision was the team's final one.

Wiki comment extraction had two real bugs the agent caught and fixed mid-run: first the comments key was mis-parsed as an empty dict (line 2616), then found to be a nested {comment, children} tree requiring recursive walking (line 4536) -- but the final wiki3.py (transcript line ~155 in the raw JSON) dedupes pages by display NAME, and the corpus visibly serves duplicate-titled pages under different ids (e.g. 'Weekly Notes — Week of Mar 31' at both id 66 and 186, lines 1736/1740). This is a plausible root cause for why g3.r1.l5 and g3.r2.s1a (both wiki page comments) never surfaced despite an otherwise careful, comment-aware wiki pass -- though it cost no fact here because both were redundantly carried by chat remarks.

The agent spent real effort matching ruff's exact pinned CI version (0.8.6) rather than trusting a newer locally-downloaded ruff (0.16.6) that flagged 142 spurious errors, comparing against a clean worktree baseline first (lines 7241-7398) -- careful provenance hygiene beyond what the ticket required.

Before marking task_complete the agent independently verified deployment by finding the actual release directory on the host filesystem (/opt/sweworld/curator/releases/20260908235747-a2d6a41) and listing its contents to confirm retry_policy.py was present, rather than trusting the CI 'green' status alone (lines 8607-8826).

12 of the 14 missed remarks were missed for the same mechanical reason: the agent's grep passes were tuned to uppercase design tokens (THROTTLE, DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS, decide, etc.), and these particular remarks are phrased in ordinary lowercase prose ('tiny backof', 'fake clock', 'sleeping a full backoff on requests we've already decided to bin') with no unique searchable token -- the agent never read those channel/days directly by any other means. None of the 9 graded facts were lost to this because the corpus's spread requirement guarantees redundant carriers.
